content:
A quick update on the linear model (including t-test), since our release of the Lindeberg CLT.

We've got the following sorry-free:

  • CLT for the linear model, under general conditions (independence, fixed design, model-robust aka assumption-lean setting)
  • consistency of variance estimation under the same conditions (HC0-HC4)
  • asymptotically valid inference (confidence intervals and hypothesis tests, including the t-test)

We haven't made the thing public yet because some of the AI-generated code is muddled or feels unnatural, if formally correct (more below).

Anyone interested in helping us with this "sanitisation" job is welcome - we'll give you access. Otherwise, we're hoping to be done in the next few weeks.

Examples of strangeness:

  • A proof used bound B at two points; we later obtain a sharper bound B', but the AI only fits this into the proof at one of the two spots (proof is still correct as we only need the sharper bound at one point, but this introduces two separate bound lemmas, which seems inefficient).
  • The AI proves intermediate results that then aren't actually used anywhere (this could be down to a revision which replaces the result with something new to fit a different proof approach).
  • General messiness with commenting - comments frequently refer to the change the AI is making at the time, but if it's replacing a previous result then we have phantom references to things that no longer exist. Plus stylistically, the AI's comments are all over the place: inconsistent numbering, inconsistent use of headers, inconsistent use of mathematical notation, etc. None of these affect the validity of results but make things more difficult for human comprehension.
  • (Perhaps pedantic) The AI will often do exactly what you tell it to, which sometimes misses some 'free wins'. For example, at one point we establish a sharp bound on the second order Taylor expansion remainder for exp(iy), when in fact the proof structure can be used to get a bound for the kth order expansion. We only need the second order for our results, but it seems like a nice Mathlib result to just have the general bound present, since it's only a line or two of extra work.

On the question of AI, I was thinking that maybe we should allow some space that the proof belongs to ai, similar idea here: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti ; but definitely we should be careful about building the wall between carefully reviewed ones and ai generated ones
